framework.name: National Standards for Family and Consumer Sciences Education 3.0 (NASAFACS), with Illinois Learning Standards for the K-5 units
framework.note: FCS codes are NASAFACS area-of-study content standards (FCS 8.2 = food safety and sanitation procedures), which are not grade-banded; K-5 units add Illinois Goal 22 health benchmarks (1 = early, 2 = late elementary) and Common Core math as adopted by Illinois. Alignment is the course author's judgment, not a certification.

standards.text: Practice basic sanitation procedures, beginning with proper hand washing.
Recognize how clean hands and surfaces help keep food safe to eat.
Identify ways to promote health and prevent illness, such as hand washing and cleanliness.
Follow basic food safety practices, such as keeping cold foods cold and hot foods hot.
Use simple kitchen tools, including sharp ones, safely and put them away properly.
Identify dangerous situations and the safety methods that reduce the risk of harm.
Recognize what foods the body needs to grow and stay healthy.
Identify what influences the food choices people make and how often they eat foods.
Identify ways to promote health and prevent illness, including healthy eating practices.
Show teamwork by taking responsibility for your part of a shared job.
Practice work-readiness habits such as following steps and finishing a task, including clean-up.
Use time and materials responsibly and return them so a job is fully done.
Measure ingredients accurately, spooning and levelling, as part of following a recipe.
Handle and prepare foods correctly by reading and following simple recipes.
Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses using standard units such as liters, grams and kilograms.
Use basic hand-sewing skills to repair an item, such as sewing on a button.
Practice simple textile construction skills, choosing a stitch by what the seam must survive.
Make simple money decisions, such as comparing prices before spending.
Manage resources like money by weighing choices between goods.
Explore how consumer choices connect to prices and the wider economic system.
Use the four operations to solve word problems involving money and other measurements.
Keep hands, food and work areas clean before, during and after cooking.
Prepare a simple food by following the steps of a recipe in order.
Plan, acquire and prepare a simple food that meets a nutrition need.
Work as a team to plan, cook and clean up a meal.
Describe and compare safety methods that reduce risks in dangerous situations, such as around heat.
Demonstrate food safety and sanitation procedures such as handwashing, avoiding cross-contamination and safe temperatures.
Evaluate the factors that affect food safety from production through consumption.
Apply risk-management procedures to food safety, food testing and sanitation.
Select, use and maintain food production equipment safely according to industry standards.
Select, use and maintain food production tools and equipment, such as knives, to industry standards.
Demonstrate professional food preparation methods and techniques, such as standard knife cuts, to produce food products.
Follow food safety and sanitation procedures while handling tools and food.
Use professional food preparation techniques, including accurate measuring and mise en place, to follow a recipe.
Apply menu-planning principles based on standardized recipes, including measurement equivalents and scaling recipes up or down.
Acquire, handle and use foods to meet the nutrition and wellness needs of individuals and families.
Demonstrate the skills needed to produce, alter or repair apparel and textile products, such as mending seams.
Demonstrate basic fashion, apparel and textile design and construction skills, such as choosing stitches.
Produce, alter or repair textile products using appropriate equipment, such as a sewing machine, and techniques.
Apply apparel and textile design skills in a constructed product.
Demonstrate transferable and employability skills, such as safe equipment use and following procedures.
Evaluate fibers, fabrics and textile products for their properties, care and uses.
Demonstrate apparel and textile design skills, applied here to grain, bias and pattern layout.
Apply construction skills to cut and produce a textile product from a pattern.
Demonstrate professional cooking methods and techniques, such as dry-heat and moist-heat cooking, across menu categories.
Use and maintain cooking equipment safely and to industry standards.
Handle and prepare foods in ways that meet nutrition and wellness needs.
Apply food safety practices, including cooking foods to safe internal temperatures.
Evaluate the nutritional needs of individuals and families in relation to health across the life span.
Acquire, handle and use foods to meet nutrition and wellness needs, including planning meals on a budget.
Analyze factors that influence nutrition and wellness practices across the life span.
Apply menu-planning principles and techniques to meet the needs of those being served.
Evaluate nutrition principles, food plans and food preparation techniques.
Evaluate nutrition principles and food preparation techniques through the science behind them.
Evaluate how science and technology influence food composition, safety and related issues.
Apply food preparation techniques with an understanding of how ingredients react during cooking.
Apply risk-management procedures to food safety and food testing, such as controlled kitchen experiments.
Analyze principles of human growth and development across the life span.
Analyze conditions that influence human growth and development, including in early childhood.
Demonstrate a safe and healthy environment for children in one's care.
Evaluate parenting and caregiving practices that maximize children's growth and development.
Demonstrate techniques for positive, collaborative relationships with children, such as guidance instead of punishment.
Demonstrate management of financial resources, such as budgeting and credit, to meet goals across the life span.
Demonstrate management of individual and family resources such as food, shelter, transportation and time.
Analyze relationships between the economic system and consumer actions, such as renting and borrowing.
Analyze policies that support consumer rights and responsibilities, such as protection from scams and fraud.
Plan a menu from standardized recipes, including cost, to meet a stated need.
Produce food products using professional preparation methods and techniques.
Produce a textile or apparel product, for students who choose the sewn capstone.
Manage resources such as money, time and materials to complete a project.
Demonstrate teamwork and leadership skills while carrying out and presenting shared work.
Demonstrate employability skills such as planning, costing, meeting a timeline and evaluating finished work.
